cognitive_capacity.rationale: All 31 samples present multiplication estimation tasks at the appropriate cognitive level for Grade 3, Quarter 3. The problems use 2- to 3-digit factors paired with 1- to 2-digit factors, requiring mental estimation by rounding to multiples of 10. No excessive visual or textual complexity beyond what the curriculum stage demands; all formats (mcq, true_false, cloze, error_detect) are developmentally appropriate for third-grade learners working with estimation strategies.

competency_alignment.rationale: Every sample directly assesses the stated competency: estimating the product of 2- to 3-digit numbers by 1- to 2-digit numbers using multiples of 10. Samples 1, 4, 5, 7, 11, 13, 15, 19, 23, 25, 27, 28 use direct estimation prompts. Samples 2, 6, 9, 12, 14, 17, 22, 29 use true/false evaluation of given estimates. Samples 3, 8, 16, 20, 21, 24, 26, 30, 31 use error-detection within student work. Each variant requires the same underlying skill: rounding factors and computing the rounded product.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: All five decomposed requirements are losslessly represented across the sample set. Rounding patterns vary systematically (e.g., 43→40, 118→120, 850→850) demonstrating multiple rounding strategies within the 10-multiple constraint. Error-detection samples extend the skill by requiring students to verify peers' estimates, which demands the same competency applied in a different cognitive frame.

decomposition.reasoning: The five requirements partition the competency without gaps or redundancy. Every sample requires estimating a product (req 1), includes at least one 2- to 3-digit factor (req 2), includes at least one 1- to 2-digit factor (req 3), demonstrates factor estimation/rounding (req 4), and rounds all factors to multiples of 10 (req 5). No sample lacks any requirement, and no requirement is absent across the full set.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The 31-sample set provides broad coverage of the competency space. Factor combinations span 10×14 (smallest factors) to 930×13, with 10-multiple rounding targets ranging from 100 to 10000. Multiple item formats (7 mcq, 9 true_false, 4 cloze, 8 error_detect, 3 hybrid themed) expose the same skill across different response modes. Two samples include thematic wrappers (baskets, basketballs) without interfering with the mathematical content, demonstrating format resilience.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All factor magnitudes fall within the stated range of 2- to 3-digit and 1- to 2-digit numbers. The smallest factor is 10 (boundary case for two-digit range); the largest is 930. True products after estimation span from 100 (10×10) to 10000 (500×20), a range appropriate for Grade 3 mental arithmetic and place-value understanding at the quarter 3 milestone. No sample requires computation beyond what estimation-by-rounding supports.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The generator produces systematic variation across response formats (mcq with distractors all within 1-2 points of the correct estimate; true_false with deliberately wrong estimates; error_detect naming student solvers; cloze with fill-in blanks). Rounding choices vary systematically: some factors round down (43→40), some round up (118→120), some remain unchanged (450→450, 930→930, 503→500). This range confirms the generator explores multiple legitimate estimation approaches within the multiples-of-10 constraint.
